About me

Understanding institutions.
Paying attention to people.

I'm a freshman at Tulane University studying political science on the pre-law track. My interests center on government, public policy, and the relationship between legal institutions and everyday life.

Growing up in New York City shaped how I think about community. Learning alongside people with different experiences taught me to listen closely, question assumptions, and consider more than one perspective.

Tulane UniversityPolitical Science · Pre-Law
02

Academic interests

Questions worth asking.

The ideas guiding my studies and the conversations I want to be part of.

I / GOVERNMENT

Power & institutions

How political institutions distribute power, shape participation, and influence whose voices are heard.

A question I'm exploring

How do the rules of political institutions affect representation and the ability to make meaningful change?

II / LAW

Law & interpretation

How legal arguments are built, how evidence is evaluated, and how interpretation shapes the application of the law.

A question I'm exploring

How can the same legal text lead to different conclusions, and what makes one interpretation more persuasive?

III / PUBLIC POLICY

Policy & everyday life

How public decisions become lived experiences, and what those experiences reveal about a policy's impact.

A question I'm exploring

How should we evaluate a policy when its benefits and costs fall differently across communities?

03

Experience

Learning through participation.

Community service · Assistant coach

Girls on the Run

Supported elementary school girls in a program centered on confidence, connection, and movement. Returning as an assistant coach after participating myself gave me a new perspective on encouragement, empathy, and leadership.

Academic involvement

Mock trial

Explored legal reasoning through mock trial, developing an interest in how evidence and interpretation come together in an argument. That experience helped shape my decision to pursue the pre-law track.

An evolving perspective
